Anya: Heads-up — CI eval for quantized-resnet-chat-2 is intermittently producing higher-entropy outputs on the same seed + prompt. Failing our regression gate ~1/10 runs.
Mike: Ugh. Is it definitely the sampler and not tokenization drift?
Anya: Tokenization checksums are stable across runs (checked). Repro pattern: run eval-runner with --seed 42 --top_p 0.9 --temp 0.8 vs identical worker pool; sometimes logits diverge after step ~12.
Sanam: Can you paste the small runner invocation and any relevant logs?
Anya: Sure:
```
./eval-runner --model quant/resnet-chat-2-int8 --seed 42 --batch-size 8 --top_p 0.9 --temperature 0.8 --worker-pool-size 4
```
log excerpt:
```
[runner] seed=42 rng_state_hash=0x7f3a4b
[worker-2] allocate KV cache seq=0
[step-12] sample(top_p=0.9) chosen=token(345) prob=0.06
[worker-2] rng_state_hash=0x1c2d9f  <-- diverged
```
Mike: The rng_state_hash change looks like the core symptom. Are workers recreating RNGs per request or reusing a global PRNG?
Raul: Runner currently uses a global std::mt19937 per worker and advances it when mixing batches; there were recent patchups to reuse worker threads to avoid cost of init. Could be reuse bug.
Sanam: Also recall that our top_p sampler calls normalize_and_shuffle which uses inplace sort on a fused tensor; quantized kernels changed the order of near-equal logits under parallel reduction. That could flip which tokens enter the top_p truncation boundary.
Anya: Good point — I saw tiny float differences after quant kernel switch, but didn't expect that to be amplified. However, amplification via sampler nondeterminism is plausible.
Mike: Two-pronged approach: (1) enforce deterministic RNG per-request (instantiate a small pcg64/philox object seeded by master seed + request id) and (2) add a CI-only strict sampler mode which uses stable arg-sorting tie-breaker (e.g., stable_sort with index tie-break).
Raul: I can prototype (1) quickly. But prophylaxis (2) sounds useful for CI to catch algorithmic nondet.
Anya: Could we also log the pre-truncation logits + top_p threshold for the failing run to see how close we are to the cutoff? That'll tell whether tiny fp shifts cause the flip.
Sanam: Agree. Also add a tokenizer checksum assert before each request and post-tokenizer length check.
ci-bot: Job 32871: eval-runner/quantization-stability — failed 1 of 10 runs (flaky). Rerun? :repeat:
Anya: Rerun doesn't always reproduce. I reproduced locally once by running a tight loop with worker-pool-size=4 and --warmup=0.
Mike: If worker reuse is the culprit, try forcing worker affinity single-threaded and see if flake goes away. That isolates concurrency vs kernel nondet.
Raul: Quick experiment: I added per-request RNG in a local patch and ran 50 iterations; zero failures so far (before it was ~10% fail). Uploading diff to GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/214
Sanam: Nice. Do we have perf hit metrics? Per-request RNG creation is cheap if we use a fast PCG and pool reuse of its internal state structure.
Raul: Measured ~+1.8% latency p50, which is acceptable for CI and maybe for canary.
Anya: Proposed next steps:
- Add pre/post logits dumps on flaky CI run (temp storage, redacted)
- Add stable tie-break option for sampler and make it CI default
- Land per-request RNG patch behind a flag (--deterministic-ci)
- Add an integration test that runs the same seed 20x with quant kernels and asserts identical outputs
Mike: Also add a test that sets top_p near boundary (like 0.9001) and asserts no divergence with tiny epsilon jitter.
Sanam: I'll add tokenizer checksum and a short unit test for quant kernel reduction determinism.
Anya: Any concern about this hiding legit model regression? If we make CI too strict it might mask small quality regressions while removing flakiness.
Mike: Make the strict mode CI-only: when flag enabled we require bitwise-equivalent outputs for seed tests. In prod default remains probabilistic.
Raul: I'll open a followup issue to audit other places that reuse RNG state (beam search, resume paths).
Anya: Cool. For immediate triage I've attached the failing run id: job://32871/attempt-3 and a minimal repro script in the PR.
Sanam: Thanks — I'll start the quant kernel determinism test and ping infra to increase CI artifacts retention for that job so we can fetch logs.
ci-bot: Job 32871: rerun triggered by @Raul.
Mike: Let's aim to have a mitigation (CI stable sampler + per-request RNG) in next 48h. If we still see fuzz after that we'll dig into kernel reduction ordering.
Anya: Thanks team. Leaving notes in the eval-runner issue tracker. :thumbsup:
